items.title: The AI Funding Loop: What Happens When the Money Stops?
items.snippet:
The assumption has been relatively simple:

Demand will keep growing, capital wi...
items.raw_snippet:
The assumption has been relatively simple:

Demand will keep growing, capital will remain available, and the returns will eventually justify the investment.

But some of the early cracks are beginning to show.

And they are appearing in places that are connected.

1.   The funding picture is changing

Consider OpenAI.

The company initially sought to raise $30bn at a hoped-for valuation of $1.4tn. [...] Its latest funding round has reportedly secured approximately $11bn in commitments so far, at a $1.25tn valuation. Its reported fundraising ambition has subsequently been reduced to around $20bn.

That is a meaningful change in investor appetite.

Then consider Anthropic.

Blackstone has reportedly warned investors that Anthropic may receive a high-yield, non-investment-grade credit rating following its IPO.

This is not an actual downgrade. It is an expectation communicated to investors. [...] Investors provide capital to AI laboratories.
    AI laboratories commit enormous sums to cloud and compute providers.
    Cloud providers purchase chips and build data centres.
    Chipmakers benefit from expanding infrastructure expenditure.
    Financial institutions provide debt and structured financing.
    The resulting growth supports higher valuations and attracts further investment.

Capital moves around the ecosystem, creating revenue, assets, commitments and valuations.

items.title: The Board's AI Question Is a Capital Allocation Question - Dawgen Global
items.snippet: Proposals compete for the same money. An AI project should be weighed against th...
items.raw_snippet:
Proposals compete for the same money. An AI project should be weighed against the other things the company could do with the same funds: a new branch, a debt repayment, a dividend. If it cannot show a better return than those, it should not be funded simply because it is AI. [...] There is a lookback. Boards routinely compare the results of past acquisitions and building projects with what was promised. AI programmes deserve the same discipline: a regular review of what each initiative actually delivered, recorded in the AI Earnings Register™ and checked independently.

None of these is new. They are the ordinary disciplines of capital allocation. The problem is that they are seldom applied to AI. [...] When the same board considers AI, those questions often disappear. AI arrives as a technology item, presented by the IT function or a vendor, discussed in the language of models, platforms and pilots. The board asks whether the company is keeping up, whether the data is secure and whether staff have been trained. It rarely asks what the shareholders will get back for their money.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

## Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview. [...] Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

## AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to: [...] TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.
